notes: Correct in both backends with very thorough tests (copy, escape, single root, ranges), but adds unnecessary complexity in squashfs New/NewObject fallbacks and in zip Open EOF special-casing.
Code matches the reference exactly, with a relevant docs section and reasonable tests covering squashfs listing/reading, a regular .rclonelink file, zip basics and the hostile-archive copy.

Clean implementation that also gives a regular .rclonelink member precedence over a colliding symlink, but squashfs reads targets by duck-typing a Readlink method instead of the library's StatT.LinkTarget, and there is no hostile-archive test.

Correct and consistent, with extensive tests and binary fixtures, but uses an unchecked StatT type assertion and adds extra zip dirtree root/parent retention plus an Open refactor beyond what was needed.
Squashfs side is fine, but zip hides every member below a symlink path even without --links, a behaviour change beyond the spec that fails a hidden test; it also changes readZip's signature.

Squashfs New now temporarily mutates f.root and sets f.file to the full remote rather than the leaf, which likely breaks single-file roots in subdirectories; zip root logic is convoluted and drops symlinks under a .rclonelink-named directory root.

Works for the main cases in both backends, but the zip root matching is convoluted and has a bug: with --links, root "foo.rclonelink" also matches a regular member "foo"; squashfs New also accepts an unsuffixed root that points at a symlink.
